questions.stem: The polar graph of r = cos(θ) is inscribed within a circle with radius 2. Which statement best describes the symmetry of the graph?

choices.B: It is symmetric about the horizontal axis only.
choices.C: It is symmetric about the vertical axis only.
choices.D: It is symmetric about both axes.

questions.solution: The polar equation r = cos(θ) describes a cardioid, which has symmetry about both the horizontal (x-axis) and vertical (y-axis) lines due to the even nature of cosine. Since it's inscribed in a circle with radius 2, the entire graph will be contained within these symmetrical axes.
questions.explanation: Cardioids have reflective symmetry along both axes because cosine is an even function.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to choose B or C, thinking that the symmetry is only along one axis. However, cosine's even nature ensures symmetry in both directions.

questions.stem: The polar equation r = 2sin(3θ) creates a rose petal graph. Which of the following statements best describes its symmetry?

choices.B: It is symmetric about the horizontal axis only.
choices.C: It is symmetric about the vertical axis only.

questions.solution: The polar equation r = a*sin(bθ) creates a rose petal graph with b petals. Since b = 3 in this case, the graph will have 3 * 2 = 6-fold rotational symmetry around the origin.
questions.explanation: Roses graphs created by r = a*sin(bθ) have rotational symmetry equal to 2b.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to choose B or C, assuming that there is linear symmetry. However, rose petals only exhibit rotational symmetry.

questions.stem: The polar equation r = 1 creates a circle with radius 1. What type of symmetry does this graph have?

choices.B: It is symmetric about the horizontal axis only.
choices.C: It is symmetric about the vertical axis only.

questions.solution: A circle has infinite rotational symmetry around its center. In this case, the origin acts as the center.
questions.explanation: Circles have infinite rotational symmetry, meaning they can be rotated any angle and still align perfectly with their original position.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to choose B or C, thinking that there is linear symmetry. However, circles only exhibit rotational symmetry.

questions.stem: The polar equation r = 2sin(4θ) creates a five-pointed star graph. Which statement best describes its symmetry?

choices.B: It is symmetric about the horizontal axis only.
choices.C: It is symmetric about the vertical axis only.

questions.solution: The polar equation r = a*sin(bθ) creates a star graph with b petals. Since b = 4 in this case, the graph will have 2b = 8-fold rotational symmetry around the origin, but only 4 of those are distinct due to symmetry.
questions.explanation: Star graphs created by r = a*sin(bθ) have rotational symmetry equal to 2b, with some symmetries overlapping.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to choose B or C, assuming that there is linear symmetry. However, star graphs only exhibit rotational symmetry.

questions.stem: The polar equation r = 2cos(θ) creates a cardioid graph. Which of the following lines will NOT pass through the center of symmetry for this graph?
questions.solution: The cardioid created by r = 2cos(θ) has symmetry about both the horizontal and vertical axes. The lines y = x and y = -x are not axes of symmetry.
questions.explanation: Cardioids have reflective symmetry along both the x-axis and y-axis, but not along oblique lines like y = x or y = -x.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to choose A or B, thinking that they represent the axes of symmetry. However, those choices are correct; the incorrect choice is C, which represents a line perpendicular to the axes of symmetry.

questions.stem: The polar equation r = 1 + cos(θ) creates a limaçon graph. Which of the following lines will pass through the center of symmetry for this graph?
questions.solution: The limaçon created by r = 1 + cos(θ) has symmetry about the horizontal axis. The line y = 0 represents the x-axis, which is an axis of symmetry.
questions.explanation: Limaçons with equations like r = a + bcos(θ) or r = a + bsin(θ), where a > |b|, have symmetry along the horizontal (x-axis).
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to choose B, C, or D, thinking that they represent axes of symmetry. However, only A is correct as it represents the x-axis.

questions.stem: The polar equation r = 2sin(θ)cos(θ) creates a lemniscate graph. Which statement best describes its symmetry?

choices.B: It is symmetric about the horizontal axis only.
choices.C: It is symmetric about the vertical axis only.

questions.solution: The polar equation r^2 = a^2sin(2θ) creates a lemniscate graph, which has 2-fold rotational symmetry around the origin. In this case, r = 2sin(θ)cos(θ) simplifies to r^2 = 4sin^2(θ)cos^2(θ), which is equivalent to the standard form.
questions.explanation: Lemniscates have 2-fold rotational symmetry around their center.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to choose B or C, assuming that there is linear symmetry. However, lemniscates only exhibit rotational symmetry.
